full_judgment: 30. To the contention of the Revenue that had the legislature intended to give exemption then it would have said so, the reply by the respondent is that there is no presumption as to impose a tax is convincing. It is settled that in a taxing Act one has to look merely at what is clearly stated. There is no room for intendment. There is no equity' about tax. "Nothing is to be read in, nothing is to be implied. One can only look fairly at the language used" (Per Rowlatt, J in Cape Brandy Syndicate Vs I.R. (1921) I. K.B. 54 approved by H.L. Canadian Eagle Oil Company Ltd. Vs- King, 27 T.C. 205.
